$comment: Zenith's half of the agent-board mapping. COMMITTED, and this repo
owns it. Everything a ticket is judged by — gate command lines,
pinned unit baselines, conventions, categories, living-doc dirs —
lives here, beside the code it judges. This file is sent to the board
with every request.
The board keeps only POLICY (the agent account, complexity->model
routing, timeouts) and may be on an entirely different machine. It
holds no path into this filesystem: `project` below declares which
board project this checkout serves, rather than a config elsewhere
declaring where the checkout lives. That inversion is the only
direction that survives the two being on separate machines.
WHY the gates live here: a ticket that ratchets against a stale pin
fails with ZERO failing tests — the unit gate asserts `ran == Baseline`
EXACTLY, so a suite that GREW reds a required check while every test
passes. A pin in another repo's gitignored file could only be
remembered; here a reviewer sees it in the same diff.
The NUMBERS themselves are no longer written here. They live in
Tools/unit_baselines.json — one unprotected home — and the gate lines
below name the GAME instead. While the number was duplicated into this
file and .github/workflows/, both protectedPaths, bumping a pin was
work the agent loop could never do, so every test-adding ticket was
unreachable.
`protectedPaths` here is DOCUMENTATION, not enforcement, and it is not
unioned with anything: `guardrailsOf` (Tools/Vault/cli/compat.mjs)
resolves protected paths as `project.protectedPaths ?? boardGuardrails
?? clientFile.protectedPaths` -- a FALLBACK CHAIN, not a union --
and `boardGuardrails` (vault.config.json's `policy.board.guardrails`,
the one the claim payload reports, mirrored into
`policy.resolved.guardrails` for `zagent guard`'s own
`checkProtectedPaths` call) is always present. So this file's list
never wins and enforces nothing on its own; the two vault.config.json
copies are the actual floor, and they must be edited by a human, same
as this file. `$`-prefixed keys are comments and are stripped.
This file is itself protected: the loop may propose changes to its
own gates as a Suggestions row, never commit them.
$lanes: Parallel /tick lanes (Docs plan: parallel `/tick` lanes; Tools/zagent/protocol/TICK.md's own
'Lane mode' section). Enabled 2026-09-23 so the ZEN and ZM lanes can be
registered (`zagent lane add`); a /tick from the main checkout still runs
the serial protocol, and only a /tick started inside a registered lane
(`zagent lane which` -> mode lane) runs lane mode. Turning lanes on was a
deliberate human commit to this file, never something a tick does to itself.
`root`: where `zagent lane add <PROJECT>` creates a lane's persistent
worktree (one per board project, never per ticket) when no `--path` is
wait row (MAIN_DIRTY / MAIN_NOT_ON_BASE / a build-slot timeout past its own
budget) before a lane gives up and Blocks `integration-conflict` instead of
waiting again. `buildSlotWaitMinutes`: how long Tools/build_lock.ps1 waits
for the one machine-wide build slot before tick_gates.ps1 exits 11 ("slot
busy") -- read by build_lock.ps1 itself, since ZenithCli reads no zagent
$conventions: UNIVERSAL only -- true of every category regardless of language, and
C++-specific half used to live in this same string and got
unconditionally pasted in front of every worker prompt including a
Node/Vitest one (Tooling); it now lives separately in
`languageConventions` below, which a category can suppress with
`suppressLanguageConventions` WITHOUT losing these two. Do not fold
`languageConventions` back in here -- that reintroduces the exact
conventions: Root CLAUDE.md is binding. Never run Sharpmake in a linked worktree unless it is a registered lane (ZEN-D-043).
$languageConventions: The C++-only half, split out from `conventions` above (2026-09-20).
Suppressed for a category via `suppressLanguageConventions: true`
(currently only Tooling, which is Node/PowerShell) -- resolveRules()
composes universal + (this unless suppressed) + the category's own,
so a suppressing category still gets the universal clauses.
Note `Build/**` joined Engine's `paths` in the same pass that added
the suppression flag: a Tooling ticket that touches a regen-adjacent
path is now MORE likely to trip "never run Sharpmake in a linked
worktree unless it is a registered lane", not less, which is exactly
why that clause had to stay universal rather than be dropped
languageConventions: No std:: containers; every .cpp starts with #include "Zenith.h"; tabs; braces on new lines; Zenith_Assert is the real assert (ZENITH_ASSERT is an empty marker).
$cleanup: Tools/sweep_game_exes.ps1 replaces the old inline Get-Process/Stop-Process one-liner, which matched by NAME ALONE across the WHOLE MACHINE -- exactly the hazard a lane makes real, since two lanes (or a lane and the main checkout) can each have their own zenithmon.exe running at once and the old line would kill both. The new script dot-sources Tools/tick_gates.ps1 -NoRun to reach Invoke-ExeSweep/Select-SweepTargets, the same path-scoped, directory-boundary-safe killer every gate phase already uses, and sweeps only THIS checkout's own tree. It is a `$`-free committed string on purpose: this array may be run by a POSIX shell OR PowerShell, and a `$` inside the committed string would be expanded by whichever shell reads it. It still always `exit 0` -- a sweep that finds nothing to sweep is a success, and a cleanup line that reports failure for the common case is a trap for anything that ever branches on the result. Lane mode skips this step entirely at its own step 9 (Tools/zagent/protocol/TICK.md's Lane mode section) -- a main-mode tick's step 9 runs after `finish` releases I5, while a lane may still be mid-build.

$comment: The gate line names the GAME, not a number. The ZM boot count lives
in Tools/unit_baselines.json — the ONE unprotected home for it. This
file and .github/workflows/zm-tests.yml are both protectedPaths, so
while the number lived here the agent loop could never bump a pin,
which made every test-adding ticket unreachable. Read it from a
NULL-config exe — a Vulkan exe reports higher for the same tree.
Zenithmon.$paths: The directories this area OWNS. A ticket filed under another category whose diff reaches one of these has THESE gates unioned into its own — see the Engine note below for the failure that motivated it.
Zenithmon.conventions: Games/Zenithmon/CLAUDE.md + Docs/AgentBriefing.md are binding. ZM_ prefix. NEVER create a branch, PR, or worktree (ZM-D-031); in lane mode only the tick itself cuts agent/<KEY> (ZM-D-224).

$comment: The gate line names the GAME, not a number. The engine boot count
(via Null Combat) lives in Tools/unit_baselines.json, which is the
ONE place it is written. A backend-neutral engine unit moves EVERY
game's row in that file, not just this one — see the conventions
string below.
$paths: Zenith/** is shared code that every game links, so a diff that
reaches it needs THESE gates whatever category the ticket was
filed under. Four consecutive tickets filed `Zenithmon` edited
Zenith/** and ran a gate list that builds one game and checks one
pin; ZM-50's own Goal said `the fix is engine-side` while the
category quietly decided otherwise, because only the category had
any mechanical effect. `zagent gates <KEY>` unions on these.
Deliberately NOT Tools/**: Tools/unit_baselines.json holds every
game's pin, so listing it would make a one-line Zenithmon pin bump
rebuild and re-test Combat. This lists the code an engine gate
actually verifies, not everything an engine ticket might touch.
Build/** belongs here, not to Tooling: it is Sharpmake — the
descriptors, the per-lib project files, the manifest codegen — and
it decides what every game compiles and which TUs land in which
lib. Measured 2026-09-20: a diff touching only
Build/Sharpmake_Zenith.cs resolved 5 gate lines and unioned in
NOTHING, the least-covered important directory in the repo, while
Zenith/ZenithECS/Zenith_Scene.h resolved 18 and Tools/doc_lint.ps1
resolved 16. A wrong Sharpmake edit is a duplicate-symbol link
break or a silently dropped TU in every game — the same
every-game blast radius the rest of this list already exists to
cover, not a Tooling-shaped concern like `npm test` or a lint
script.
$gates: EVERY GAME IS COMPILED, and that is the point of this list.
Games/Combat references Zenith_TerrainComponent in ZERO source files,
while Zenithmon references it in 12, CityBuilder in 4 and RenderTest in
4. So when ZEN-5 made members of that header private, all four of the
gates this list used to hold went green while three games could have
been left un-compilable. Nobody would have known until somebody built
That is the ZM-50 failure from the other direction, and the `paths`
union above cannot catch it: the diff is inside Engine's OWN paths, so
there is no foreign category to pull in. A public header's blast radius
is everything that INCLUDES it, which no directory mapping expresses.
Builds come before tests deliberately -- a compile break in any game
should stop the run before a minute goes into Combat's suite.
Test-ZagentClient.ps1 asserts every game with a .zproj appears here, so
adding a game to the repo and forgetting this list FAILS rather than
$docLint: ★ ZEN-D-006. doc_lint's Check 7 (Check-LivePin) reconciles a game's
Status.md LIVE PIN block against Tools/unit_baselines.json, and NO
Engine gate ran doc_lint for any game -- so the one check written to
catch pin-narration drift was unreachable from exactly the tickets
that cause it. A backend-neutral engine unit moves EVERY game's row,
so engine tickets change the most pins and linted none of them.
Measured: Zenithmon's LIVE PIN sat at 4551/2698/2801 while the
manifest already held 4556/2703/2806 -- five units of un-narrated
drift accumulated since ZEN-12. C7 would have failed the moment it
ran. ZEN-40 ran it only by luck, because its diff happened to touch
Games/Zenithmon/Docs/ and unioned the Zenithmon category in.
Two games, not five: these are the two with a narrated LIVE PIN. The
pair costs ~4s against a list that takes ten minutes. The other three
are linted by the Tooling category, which owns doc_lint.ps1 itself.
Engine.conventions: Engine work moves EVERY game's pinned unit count if it adds a backend-neutral engine unit - the ticket's Definition of Done must list every pinned site, and doc_lint's C7 will red if a game's Status.md LIVE PIN block is left behind.
$decisionLog: Before this, Engine was the only non-Zenithmon category and the ONLY
one with no decisionLog/decisionIdPrefix of its own, so
`category?.decisionLog ?? project.decisionLog` fell through to a
project-level key that has never existed in this file — resolving to
undefined for every ZEN ticket. Measured, not hypothetical: ZEN-6's
DoD asked for a ruling to be recorded in the decision log and the
claim payload came back `decisionLog: null`; ZEN-19's governing
constraint had to be assembled by hand because nothing pointed at
it. A ruling recorded only on the board is invisible to a loop
worker, which has no shell and no network and reads the log off
disk with the Read tool.
Prefix verified against what is already minted: ZEN-D-003, 004,
006, 010-015 all appear in Zenith/Docs/Board/tickets/*.md, so
`ZEN-D-` is the live prefix, not a guess. Those earlier rulings
predate this file's existence (2026-09-20) and are recorded only in
those ticket bodies and the Vault's decisions database — they are
NOT backfilled into Zenith/Docs/EngineDecisionLog.md, which starts
empty; entries from here on land in both places.
No top-level project-wide decisionLog/decisionIdPrefix fallback was
added. Each category below that isn't Zenithmon or Engine either
files on a DIFFERENT board project (DevilsPlayground -> DP,
Undervault -> UV, Hearth -> HE, Foundry -> FD) or has no board
project of its own (ScriptTest, inheriting ZEN). A single ZEN-D-
fallback would misattribute a DP/UV/HE/FD ruling into the engine's
log under the wrong prefix — DevilsPlayground already has its own
Games/DevilsPlayground/Docs/DecisionLog.md, but its entries carry
no ID convention at all (checked: no `DP-D-NNN` anywhere in it),
so declaring a DP decisionIdPrefix here would invent a convention
the file doesn't follow rather than record one that exists. Each
area gets its own explicit declaration when it earns one, the same
way Zenithmon already has and Engine now does.

DevilsPlayground.$comment: Vault uses the project's direct single-checkout policy for DP. Docs/CIPolicy.md retains the historical remote branch-protection record; it does not require agent branches or PRs.
DevilsPlayground.conventions: Games/DevilsPlayground/Docs are binding; no paid/external services.

$comment: No `project` key, so tickets land on the checkout default (ZEN), and no
`branching` key, so they inherit the project's `direct` mode -- this game
is a scripting testbed for the engine, not an area with its own board.
NO run_unit_gate.ps1 line, and deliberately NO ScriptTest row in
Tools/unit_baselines.json: Test_UnitBaselineManifest.ps1 asserts every row
there is named by some workflow's -Game or declared advisory with a reason,
so an ungated row cannot be added silently. ScriptTest's coverage is its
automated tests, which `test ScriptTest --headless` runs.
The build line also appears in the Engine category above -- an engine
change compiles EVERY game, and Test-ZagentClient.ps1 fails if a game with
a .zproj is missing from that list.
ScriptTest.conventions: Games/ScriptTest/CLAUDE.md is binding. ST_ prefix. ZERO gameplay C++: the game defines no game ECS component and no game graph-node implementation -- every behaviour is an engine-owned node wired by a BuildGraph_ST_* builder in ScriptTest.cpp. ST_NoGameExtensionsContract enforces that mechanically; adding either is a redesign, not a fix. Every string two things must agree on lives once in ScriptTest_Graphs.h.

$comment: NO GATE RAN NON-C++ CODE BEFORE THIS CATEGORY EXISTED, and two of the
three tickets in the 2026-09-20 /tick audit proved it. ZEN-79's whole
deliverable was Vitest coverage in Tools/Vault; ZEN-8's was a doc_lint
check plus a Tools/Test_*.ps1 assert script. Both went GREEN on the
Engine list -- eleven C++ game builds and Combat's suite -- having
executed ZERO lines of their own diff. The only real verification in
either case was a hand-run `npm test` / assert script.
No `project` key, so tickets file on the checkout default (ZEN) and
inherit `direct` branching. This category exists mostly to be UNIONED
in: any diff touching the paths below pulls these gates whatever the
ticket was filed as.
THE PATHS ARE SCOPED, NOT `Tools/**`, and the exclusions are the point:
* `Tools/unit_baselines.json` is deliberately NOT matched. It holds
every game's pin, and a one-line bump must not drag a 5-minute
Vault suite behind it -- the same reasoning that keeps Tools/**
out of the Engine category's paths.
* `Tools/Middleware/**` is vendored third-party source (freetype,
imgui). `Tools/*.ps1` is single-segment on purpose so it cannot
reach into it.
Verified against the real selector in cli/legacy-pure/routing.mjs, not
a reimplementation of its glob matcher.
Every line below was observed green on 2026-09-20 before being added.
A gate list that starts red is a gate list people learn to ignore.
`suppressLanguageConventions: true` (below): resolveRules() in
cli/legacy-pure/routing.mjs used to ALWAYS concatenate the root
project's conventions -- universal AND C++ together, as one string
-- in front of a category's own, unconditionally. So a Tools/Vault
Node/Vitest ticket's prompt opened with "No std:: containers;
every .cpp starts with #include \"Zenith.h\"; tabs; braces on new
lines" and only THEN gave this category's own conventions below,
which say the opposite where they overlap — "Tools/Vault is Node:
ESM .mjs, Vitest... and NOT the engine's C++ naming rules". Under
I3 everything pasted becomes the worker's verbatim instructions,
and a worker has no shell and no board with which to tell which
half is current.
The fix is NOT to drop the root text wholesale -- the root
`conventions` string also carries two clauses that have nothing to
do with C++ and are just as binding on a Tooling worker: "Root
CLAUDE.md is binding" and "Never run Sharpmake in a linked
worktree unless it is a registered lane" (reworded from "in a
worktree" when parallel lanes landed -- see the `conventions` key
itself for the live text). Dropping the first tells a Tooling
worker the opposite of what is meant, and the second got MORE
reachable from here, not less, once
Build/** joined Engine's paths above -- a Tools/ ticket that
touches a regen path is exactly the shape that trips it. So the
root string is split in two: `conventions` (universal, ALWAYS
emitted) and `languageConventions` (C++-only, see its own
$comment). This flag suppresses ONLY `languageConventions` for
this category; the universal clauses and this category's own
conventions below still compose in. Every other category leaves
this unset (default false) and keeps getting universal + language
+ its own, unchanged from before the split.
Tooling.conventions: Tools/ is the asset bake plus the agent-loop tooling; Tools/CLAUDE.md is binding for the bake. PowerShell here follows the surrounding scripts (Set-StrictMode -Version Latest, $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop', a printed assertion count, exit 0/1) and NOT the engine's C++ naming rules. Tools/Vault is Node: ESM .mjs, Vitest, the helpers under Tools/Vault/test/helpers. A doc_lint check runs against EVERY game, so a change to one must be proven against all five.

$comment: Project UV. THE BOOTSTRAP STATE: Games/Undervault has docs (GDD + TDD)
but no .zproj, so the permanent gates below cannot compile anything yet --
and that is the mechanism, not a gap. They FAIL until the first scaffold
ticket lands its .zproj + directories, and pass exactly when the scaffold
is real: the gate list IS the scaffold's acceptance test, and it needs no
protected-path edit, ever. See Docs/OperateBoard.md (the previous board's repo) for the
full bootstrap transition, including the two HUMAN edits that follow a
scaffold: a `build <Name>` line joins the Engine list above (a .zproj'd
game missing from it fails Test-ZagentClient.ps1), and the game's
baseline row joins Tools/unit_baselines.json when its first units land.
Undervault.conventions: Games/Undervault/Docs (GDD + TDD) are binding for design; the TDD's UV_ prefix and determinism rules (section 4) bind code once the scaffold lands. Branching inherited: direct; never a branch/PR/worktree (in lane mode only the tick itself cuts agent/<KEY>, ZEN-D-043).

$comment: Project HE. Same bootstrap state as Undervault: docs, no .zproj. The
gates pass exactly when the scaffold lands; see the Undervault comment.
Hearth.conventions: Games/Hearth/Docs (GDD + TDD) are binding for design; the TDD's testing strategy (section 13) binds code once the scaffold lands. Branching inherited: direct.

$comment: Project FD. Games/Foundry carries a .zproj (the static visual study,
commit 84e2fd12), so these gates compile; `test Foundry --headless` is
RED on a fresh checkout because the study's assets are Blender output
and gitignored. The board's first ticket (M0-01) replaces the study with
the TDD architecture skeleton and turns the gates green. The TDD's
L0-only + no-float lint (section 2) is the convention that scaffold
installs as CLAUDE.md before any SimCore code lands. The unit-gate,
doc-lint and SimCore-lint lines join this list by the human edit the
board's M0-16 ticket describes, once the scaffold has landed.
Roadmap: Games/Foundry/Docs/Roadmap.md carries every board key.
Foundry.conventions: Games/Foundry/Docs (GDD + TDD) are binding for design. The TDD's engine-change register (section 19) is the gate list for any engine-side work it names. Branching inherited: direct.

$comment: Every CLAUDE.md in the repo (root + every leaf module), mirrored
into its own Notion section — separate from the per-game Docs trees
above, and PROJECT-wide rather than one category's. Kept in sync by
the tick's step 9 (see tick.md) whenever a ticket's diff touches a
Docs/** path or any CLAUDE.md.
